cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: The English legal system is based on common law (judge-made law) and statute law (Acts of Parliament)

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Parliament is the supreme law-making body — parliamentary sovereignty means no Parliament can bind its successors

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: The court hierarchy ensures that lower courts follow the decisions of higher courts (doctrine of precedent)

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the UK for civil and criminal matters

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Legal personnel include judges, magistrates, solicitors, barristers and legal executives

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Judges are independent — they are not controlled by the government and must decide cases impartially

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Magistrates are unpaid volunteers who hear around 95% of criminal cases in the Magistrates' Court

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Solicitors advise clients, prepare cases and can now represent clients in all courts

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Barristers specialise in courtroom advocacy and give specialist legal opinions

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: The legal system aims to be fair, accessible and efficient — but access to justice remains a concern

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: Legal aid provides funding for those who cannot afford legal representation

cards.front: Recall a key point about The English Legal System
cards.back: The rule of law means everyone, including the government, is subject to the law

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — the english legal system?
cards.back: 1. For The English Legal System questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing The English Legal System 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
